length_format.rationale: The brief has 12 Headlines bullets, within the 8-15 range, and 10 deep-dives (Research 4, Benchmarks 1, Products 1, Industry 2, Policy 2), which sits exactly at the top of the 5-10 range. All five tiered sections are present, so no empty sections needed omitting, and the extra headline-only section for the two leftover headlines is a reasonable addition. The main deviation is deep-dive length: most items run 5-6 sentences, but three (OpenGCUA, CERT-In, Anthropic midterms) run 7 sentences, slightly over the 3-6 target, and several sentences are long and compound. This is a mild over-shoot that loosens the format, not a structural failure.
length_format.evidence: The CERT-In deep-dive runs 7 sentences, from 'India's Computer Emergency Response Team says it received several voluntary disclosures...' through 'TechCrunch notes this is the first case...' and the closing 'Why it matters...'. The OpenGCUA and Anthropic items are also 7 sentences each.

dedup.rationale: Only two of today's stories connect to prior editions, and both carry explicit 'Follow-up' labels naming the prior dates. Both add substantial new information. The CERT-In advisory is a new event that extends the agent-containment thread from the 2026-10-16 FTC item. The Axios piece adds Gartner impairment forecasts, FT debt-issuance figures and Jamie Dimon's credit tightening to the financing thread from the 2026-10-15 sell-off item and the 2026-10-16 Kospi follow-up. One minor weakness: the Axios item restates two earlier facts as context without citing the 2026-10-15 brief for them (CoreWeave's ~15% drop and Anthropic's positive Q3 cash flow). The other ten stories (Beam, Glimpse, OpenGCUA, Magnetar, RealtimeBench, Replit, Anthropic midterms, PostgreSQL 19, AWS AgentCore, TAMM Global) do not appear in any prior edition.
dedup.evidence: "Wall Street tightens on the debt-funded AI buildout as Gartner warns of impairments (October 16, 2026) — Follow-up: the financing thread in the 2026-10-15 brief's memory-chip sell-off item and the 2026-10-16 Kospi follow-up"; new data includes "$23 billion in global AI-related debt issuance in September, down from $113 billion in June".
